facts.statement: Kinnareemimus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, approximately between 125 and 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous ~125 to 120 Ma - Late

facts.statement: The species name khonkaenensis honors Khon Kaen Province in northeastern Thailand, where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific epithet is after Khon Kaen Province, which is in northeastern Thailand, where the remains of the animal were discovered.

facts.statement: Kinnareemimus was formally described in 2009 by Eric Buffetaut, Varavudh Suteethorn, and Haiyan Tong.
facts.quote: Kinnareemimus received a formal species description in 2009 when Eric Buffetaut, Varavudh Suteethorn, and Haiyan Tong published an anatomical monograph in the bulletin of the Geological Society of London.

facts.statement: The genus name Kinnareemimus means 'Kinnaree mimic', referencing a Thai folklore creature with a human upper body and bird legs.
facts.quote: When it was described, the authors named the genus after Kinnaree, a being from the folklore of the Thai people which has the head and torso of a woman and the legs of a bird and lives in the legendary Himmapan Forest.

facts.statement: Later estimates suggest Kinnareemimus was about 1.8 meters long and weighed approximately 13 kilograms.
facts.quote: It has subsequently been estimated by Molina-Pérez and Larramendi to have been about 1.8 m long and would have possibly weighed around 13 kg.

facts.statement: Kinnareemimus is distinguished by a semi-arctometatarsalian condition where the third metatarsal remains visible from the front and narrows before flaring into a triangular shape at the tip.
facts.quote: This specimen was used to diagnose Kinnareemimus as distinct from all other ornithomimosaurs based on the following apomorphies: a semi-arctometatarsalian condition where the third metatarsal is still visible in proximal view and which narrows in the distal direction before flaring into a wider triangular cross-section at the distal-most end.

facts.statement: In 2024, the diagnosis was updated to include ventrally flattened toe claws with flexor fossae, reinforcing its classification within ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: This diagnosis was amended in 2024 by Samathi to include ventrally flattened pedal unguals with flexor fossae, which supported the inclusion of Kinnareemimus within ornithomimosauria.

facts.statement: Evidence of unfused sutures suggests that at least some of the preserved vertebrae came from a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: The neural arch for the vertebra is not preserved and the portion of the bone missing corresponds to the location of the unfused sutures in an immature individual, which led the authors to suggest the specimen came from a juvenile individual.

facts.statement: Varying degrees of fusion in the preserved tail vertebrae indicate the fossils represent individuals of different ages.
facts.quote: The seven vertebrae preserved from other parts of the tail display varying degrees of fusion, indicating these specimens are from a multi-age assemblage.

facts.statement: Multiple metatarsal bones from different individuals allow for a reasonably precise reconstruction of the foot structure.
facts.quote: The metatarsals of several individuals are known, which allows the metatarsus to be reconstructed with reasonable precision.

facts.statement: Kinnareemimus is known from very incomplete remains including vertebrae, parts of the pubic bones, metatarsals, and an incomplete fibula.
facts.quote: Es conocido por restos muy incompletos que incluyen vértebras, partes de los huesos púbicos, metatarsales y una fibula incompleta.

facts.statement: The third metatarsal of Kinnareemimus exhibits a lateral pinch known as the arctometatarsalian condition, a trait also seen in ornithomimosaurs, tyrannosaurs, troodontids, and ceratosaurs.
facts.quote: El tercer metatarsal exhibe el pellizco lateral conocida como la condición "arctometarsaliana", cuyas variantes se ven en ornitomimosaurianos, tiranosáuridos, trodóntidos y cenagnátidos.

facts.statement: The name Kinnareemimus was first mentioned in a 1999 work by Sasithorn Kamsupha and as Ginnareemimus in a 2000 publication by Ryuichi Kaneko.
facts.quote: El nombre "Kinnareemimus" fue por primera vez mencionado en un trabajo de 1999 por Sasithorn Kamsupha y como "Ginnareemimus" en una publicación de Ryuichi Kaneko en 2000.

facts.statement: The genus Kinnareemimus was named by Buffetaut and colleagues in 2009.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Buffetaut et al., 2009

facts.statement: Kinnareemimus lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 135 to 130 million years ago, from the Valanginian to the Hauterivian.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 135 a 130 millones de años, desde el Valanginiense al Hauteriviense

facts.statement: Kinnareemimus lived in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The remains of Kinnareemimus were found in Thailand.
facts.quote: en Tailandia, lugar donde se encontraron los restos

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Kinnareemimus as the Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Sao Khua Formation, where Kinnareemimus fossils were found, consists of sediments indicating a fluvial environment with lakes, floodplains, and braided channels.
facts.quote: The sediments of the Sao Khua Formation are composed of red clays, mudstones, sandstones, siltstones, and conglomerate rocks, which indicate a fluvial environment which also possessed lakes, floodplains, and braided channels.

facts.statement: The estimated tarsus length in Kinnareemimus was comparable to Garudimimus but substantially smaller than the ratios seen in Struthiomimus and Gallimimus, which are believed to be well-adapted for running.
facts.quote: The estimated length of the tarsus in Kinnareemimus was comparable to the known remains of Garudimimus, and was substantially smaller than the ratios known from Struthiomimus and Gallimimus, which are believed to have been well-adapted for running.

facts.statement: Recent analyses have found very little support for classifying Kinnareemimus as an ornithomimosaur in major phylogenetic studies.
facts.quote: In his analysis, he remarks that there had been very little support for Kinnareemimus as an ornithomimosaur in the major phylogenetic analyses.

facts.statement: There is significant debate regarding the classification of Kinnareemimus, with studies suggesting it could be a basal coelurosaur, a tyrannosauroid, or an alvarezsauroid.
facts.quote: Brusatte and colleagues (2014) remarked that it was probably a basal coelurosaur. Hartman and colleagues (2019) found it as a tyrannosauroid, but also support for it possibly representing an alvarezsauroid.

facts.statement: The genus name Kinnareemimus refers to the kinnara, a creature from Hindu mythology represented in Thailand with a female body and bird legs, alluding to the animal's bird-like feet.
facts.quote: fue nombrada en referencia a kinnara, criatura de la mitología hinduista que en Tailandia, lugar donde se encontraron los restos, se la representa con cuerpo de mujer y patas de aves

facts.statement: Kinnareemimus may be the oldest known ornithomimosaur, depending on the age of the Sao Khua Formation.
facts.quote: Puede ser el ornitomimosauriano más antiguo conocido, dependiendo de la edad de la Formación Sao Khua.
